raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
Fixes #43418

## Summary

`SGLDiffusion Generate Image` (server mode) gets a `num_images` input, 1 to 10, default 1, so existing workflows behave the same.

- The count is sent as the image API's `n` in one request (generation and edit both accept it; the server caps it at 10).
- All returned images are decoded in order into one ComfyUI `IMAGE` batch. Before, the node kept only `data[0]`.
- Seeds: the server gives image `i` the seed `seed + i`, so the same settings and seed reproduce the same ordered batch. A seed of `-1` sends no seed and the server picks a random one. Documented in the README.
- Clear errors when the server returns fewer images than requested, when the images have different sizes and cannot be batched, or when `num_images` is out of range (checked before any request).

Contact sheets and speed claims are out of scope, as agreed in the issue.

## Tests

`test/unit/test_comfyui_server_image_batch.py` (new, 7 tests, CPU): default still sends `n=1` and returns a 1-image batch; `num_images=3` sends `n=3` and returns an ordered `[3, H, W, 3]` batch; fewer images than requested; mismatched sizes; out-of-range counts rejected without a request; the node exposes the input. All 7 fail against the current `nodes.py` and pass with this change. The rest of `test/unit/test_comfyui_*.py` is unchanged (the 2 `test_comfyui_profile.py` flux failures also happen on main in my CPU-only environment).

## GPU check

Ran the node against a real `sglang serve` server built from this branch on one L40S (512x512).

Anima (`circlestone-labs/anima-base-v1.0-diffusers`, 20 steps, cfg 4):
- `num_images=1` returns `[1, 512, 512, 3]` float32, `num_images=3` returns `[3, 512, 512, 3]` with three different images.
- The same request twice gives an identical batch (max diff 0.0), so order is stable.
- Batch image 1 shows the same image as a single run with seed 43, so image `i` uses `seed + i`. Pixels differ slightly from the single run, as expected for batched vs single generation.
- `num_images=11` is rejected before any request.

Z-Image-Turbo (`Tongyi-MAI/Z-Image-Turbo`): `n=1` works, but the server itself returns 500 for `n>1` ("Z-Image expects one caption embedding per image, got N images and 1 captions", from `zimage.py` `patchify_and_embed`). This happens with a direct API call too, so it is a server-side Z-Image bug, not part of this PR.

So the node is model agnostic: if the server supports `n>1` for a model, you get a proper batch, otherwise the node raises the server's own error.

nodes.body:
Exact inputs and outputs for the Anima GPU check (branch at 6b588fa, one L40S).

Server: `sglang serve --model-type diffusion --model-path circlestone-labs/anima-base-v1.0-diffusers --port 30000` (ready in 133s)

Shared node inputs: prompt `"a red fox sitting in fresh snow, photo"`, `width=512`, `height=512`, `steps=20`, `cfg=4.0`

Direct API (`POST /v1/images/generations`, `size="512x512"`, `seed=42`, `num_inference_steps=20`, `guidance_scale=4.0`, `response_format="b64_json"`):

| `n` | status | images returned |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | 200 | 1 |
| 3 | 200 | 3 |

Node (`SGLDiffusionGenerateImage.generate_image`):

| inputs | output shape | dtype | time |
|---|---|---|---|
| `seed=42` (num_images default 1) | `[1, 512, 512, 3]` | float32 | 3.06s |
| `seed=42, num_images=3` (run A) | `[3, 512, 512, 3]` | float32 | 3.91s |
| `seed=42, num_images=3` (run B) | `[3, 512, 512, 3]` | float32 | 3.89s |
| `seed=43` | `[1, 512, 512, 3]` | float32 | 2.93s |
| `seed=1, num_images=11` | `ValueError: num_images must be between 1 and 10, got 11` (no request sent) | | |

Comparisons (max abs pixel diff, values in 0..1):

| pair | max diff |
|---|---|
| run A image 0 vs image 1 | 1.0 |
| run A image 1 vs image 2 | 1.0 |
| run A vs run B (whole batch) | 0.0 |
| run A image 0 vs single `seed=42` | 0.839 |
| run A image 1 vs single `seed=43` | 0.471 |

The three batch images are different, and repeating the request gives the same batch in the same order. Batch image 1 shows the same fox and pose as the single `seed=43` run, so image `i` uses `seed + i`. The small pixel differences from the single runs come from batched vs single generation.

files.patch:
@@ -33,7 +33,7 @@ Connect to a standalone SGLang Diffusion server.
 1. **Start SGLang Diffusion Server**: Ensure the server is running and accessible.
 2. **Connect to Server**: Use the `SGLDiffusion Server Model` node to connect (default: `http://localhost:3000/v1`).
 3. **Generate Content**:
-   - `SGLDiffusion Generate Image`: For text-to-image and image editing.
+   - `SGLDiffusion Generate Image`: For text-to-image and image editing. Set `num_images` (1 to 10) to get several images from one request as one `IMAGE` batch, in order. Image `i` uses `seed + i`, so the same settings and seed reproduce the same batch; a seed of `-1` lets the server pick a random seed.
    - `SGLDiffusion Generate Video`: For text-to-video and image-to-video.
    - `SGLDiffusion Generate MiniMax-H3`: For joint video-and-audio on a standalone server.
 4. **LoRA Support**: Use `SGLDiffusion Server Set LoRA` and `SGLDiffusion Server Unset LoRA`.

@@ -28,6 +28,28 @@ def _enable_gguf_in_diffusion_models() -> None:
     resolve_video_path,
 )
 
+# The server clamps n to this range (image_api.py).
+MAX_SERVER_IMAGES = 10
+
+
+def _decode_image_batch(response: dict, num_images: int) -> torch.Tensor:
+    """Decode the server's images, in order, into one ComfyUI IMAGE batch."""
+    items = [item.get("b64_json") for item in response.get("data") or []]
+    if not items or not all(items):
+        raise RuntimeError("No image data in response")
+    if len(items) < num_images:
+        raise RuntimeError(
+            f"Requested {num_images} images but the server returned {len(items)}"
+        )
+    images = [convert_b64_to_tensor_image(b64) for b64 in items[:num_images]]
+    shapes = {tuple(image.shape[1:]) for image in images}
+    if len(shapes) > 1:
+        raise RuntimeError(
+            f"Server returned images of different sizes {sorted(shapes)}; "
+            "they cannot be combined into one IMAGE batch"
+        )
+    return torch.cat(images, dim=0)
+

         }
